sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10, 246 PDF pages (author-published undergraduate textbook; signature (+---) converted to (-+++))
sources.locator: Section 1.3 'Measurement' pp. 23-27 (1.3.1 Invariants, 1.3.2 The metric, 1.3.3 The gamma factor), Section 1.4 'The Lorentz transformation' pp. 30-31, and Chapter 2 'Foundations (optional)' sections 2.1-2.5 pp. 43-51; the reader ledger records all ten chapters read, and the load-bearing sections above were read in the extracted text

contents.name: Section 1.3.1 'Invariants': light-rectangle area, gliding-clock proper time, and the area-based derivation of the interval t^2 - x^2
contents.reason: The area-based operational derivation of the invariant interval is motivational context; the formulated framework adopts the Lorentz form, orientation, time orientation and clock interpretation as primitives rather than deriving them from area and symmetry postulates.

contents.name: Section 1.3.2 'The metric': g(u,v) = u_t v_t - u_x v_x - u_y v_y - u_z v_z, signature (+---), and the SI/natural-unit variants of Example 5
contents.support: The metric is absorbed into the model definition with the stated conversion from signature (+---) to (-+++) and with x^0 = ct fixed by the unit conventions of this page.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 'The gamma factor': time dilation, the gamma factor 1/sqrt(1-v^2), and Examples 7-10 (Pioneer 10, atomic clocks, muons)
contents.reason: Time dilation and the gamma factor are statements about clocks carried along worldlines; they belong to the clock/proper-time development, and the empirical examples are secondary narrative, not primary-report data.

contents.name: Section 1.3.4 and the interstellar road-trip Example 8: length contraction
contents.reason: Length measurement presupposes simultaneity and radar protocols; the observer-measurements page defines those and proves the length transformation, so the material is not repeated among the primitives.

contents.name: Section 1.4 'The Lorentz transformation': equation (1) t' = gamma(t - vx), x' = -v gamma t + gamma x, the light-speed-line and determinant-one checks, and Examples 11-12
contents.reason: The transformation formulas, their inverse and composition, and the invariance of the interval and cones are the subject of the next SR page, which proves them from the affine model built here.

contents.name: Section 2.1 'Causality': the arrow of time, initial-value problems, and the modest causality postulate P1
contents.reason: These are foundational discussions about how to axiomatize causality; this formulation adopts the affine model with a chosen time orientation directly and retains no deduction of P1 from a physical arrow-of-time principle.

contents.name: Section 2.2 'Flatness': failure of parallelism, parallel transport, the flatness postulate P2, and the Gravity Probe B discussion
contents.reason: Path-dependence of parallel transport is a curvature statement belonging to the general-relativity material; the special-relativity framework adopts the flat affine model without deriving flatness from transport experiments.

contents.name: Section 2.3 'Additional postulates' P3-P6 and Section 2.4 'Other axiomatizations' (Einstein's E1-E2, the T-system, and the comparison of P/E/T)
contents.reason: Reconstruction of the affine Lorentz framework from the verbal symmetry postulates is reserved to the Lorentz-transformations page's remark on the reconstruction obligations; the primitives page adopts the geometry outright.

contents.name: Section 2.5: spacetime area is a relativistic invariant, and Chapter 2 Problems 1-5
contents.reason: The area-invariance argument and its exercises are not load-bearing for the model; the determinant-one and interval-invariance statements are proved directly on the Lorentz-transformations page instead.

contents.name: Topology remark (p. 48): flatness permits nontrivial topology such as a cylinder or Moebius strip
contents.reason: This framework fixes a global inertial chart and hence A isomorphic to R^4; general flat non-simply-connected Lorentz manifolds are outside the declared scope of the special-relativity framework.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), 238 PDF pages; the reader ledger records all eight chapters read
sources.locator: Chapter 1 'Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime', printed pp. 2-7 (PDF pp. 9-14): inertial coordinates, events, the interval, the metric and coordinate changes, the Lorentz group, rotations and boosts, light cones

contents.name: Inertial frame built from rigid rods and synchronized clocks; events characterized by coordinates (t,x,y,z)
contents.reason: The operational construction and synchronization of inertial coordinates is the subject of the observer-measurements page, which supplies the radar protocol and proves its equivalence with the chart.

contents.name: The spacetime interval s^2 = -(c dt)^2 + (dx)^2 + (dy)^2 + (dz)^2 with a fixed conversion factor c (equations 1.3-1.4)
contents.support: Absorbed as the interval of the affine model; the numerical value of c is treated as an empirical parameter in the unit conventions.

contents.name: Invariance of the interval under changes of inertial frame (equation 1.4)
contents.reason: The invariance theorem requires the Lorentz transformations and the cone preservation proved on the Lorentz-transformations page; the primitives page only fixes the form of the interval.

contents.name: Coordinates x^0 = ct, x^1, x^2, x^3, the metric eta = diag(-1,1,1,1), and the summation convention (equations 1.5-1.9)
contents.support: The coordinate normalization and the diagonal component matrix are recorded in the unit and coordinate conventions item.

contents.name: Translations, general linear coordinate changes, the Lorentz group O(3,1), rotations, boosts with rapidity, and the Poincare group (equations 1.10-1.21)
contents.reason: The Lorentz group, its generators, the boost formula and the Poincare group are constructed and verified on the Lorentz-transformations page as the first consumer of the affine primitives.

contents.name: Invariance of light cones under Lorentz transformations
contents.reason: Cone invariance is proved with the transformation theorem on the Lorentz-transformations page; here only the future cone is fixed as primitive structure.

contents.name: Timelike, spacelike and null separated events classified by the sign of the interval; no absolute simultaneity
contents.support: The sign classification of displacements is the causal classification item; the physical event-pair reading is fixed by the model definition. Simultaneity clauses travel with the deferred radar material.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Mathematical Tripos Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages; same document as https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf, served by the Internet Archive because the original host fails TLS chain verification from this environment (retrieved copy sha256 fe8a24c67e884ff141f85ce192f16639ff68be6f3e60f42ba5f26b9c6af8a66a, identical to the reader copy)
sources.locator: Section 2.1 'Definition' printed pp. 24-26 and Section 2.2 'Lorentzian signature' printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 26-29): metric tensor conventions, Minkowski metric, orthonormal bases, Lorentz transformations, and the causal classification of vectors

contents.name: Section 2.1: smooth metric tensor field, signature conventions, the Minkowski metric eta = -(dx^0)^2 + (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2, and inertial frames
contents.support: The signature, metric component matrix and inertial-frame terminology are absorbed into the model definition.

contents.name: Section 2.1: inverse metric and the induced isomorphisms lowering and raising indices
contents.reason: Index raising and lowering with eta belong to the tensor and covector transformation material proved on the Lorentz-transformations page, which supplies the covector and derivative laws.

contents.name: Section 2.2: existence of an orthonormal basis with g(e_mu,e_nu) = diag(-1,1,...,1) at each point
contents.support: The orthonormal-basis lemma proves the finite-dimensional existence statement used by the frame definitions.

contents.name: Section 2.2: orthonormal bases are related by Lorentz transformations, eta_{mu nu} A^mu_rho A^nu_sigma = eta_{rho sigma} (equations 2.9-2.10)
contents.reason: The characterization of basis changes by the Lorentz condition is proved with the group and transformation theorems of the Lorentz-transformations page.

contents.name: Section 2.2: definitions of timelike, null, spacelike and causal vectors
contents.support: The sign classification is the causal classification item; the zero-vector exclusion and the causal union are stated there.

contents.name: Section 2.2: the double light cone separates timelike from spacelike vectors, and causal vectors fall into two disconnected sets
contents.support: The components lemma proves the two-component structure and its orthonormal-coordinate description, including the closed-cone description used by the time orientation.

contents.name: Section 2.2 Exercise: for nonzero orthogonal vectors, a timelike one forces the other spacelike, a null one forces the other spacelike or null, and a spacelike one leaves all possibilities
contents.support: The worked example proves the timelike case in coordinates; the null case is the companion counterexample and shows the exact failure of positive definiteness.
